name: The Walrus and the Carpenter
desc: Closing the loop where it opened

name: Taylor Shellfish Oyster Bar
desc: Their own Puget Sound farms — order a mixed dozen and compare

name: Elliott's Oyster House
desc: Touristy but genuinely good, and right by the water

name: Shake Shack South Lake Union
desc: Gluten-free bun, no cheese, and say “clean prep” — the regular buns are buttered on the same surface.

name: Munchen Haus
desc: Bratwurst — ask about milk powder in the sausage, it is often there

name: Chico Hot Springs
desc: Game meats, done properly. Mention the allergies when booking

name: Local Bar and Grill
desc: Elk, bison and wagyu in one sitting

name: Snake River Grill
desc: The one splurge dinner, if you want one

name: In-N-Out Burger
desc: Protein style, no cheese. The fries are safe — own fryer, potato and sunflower oil only

name: Crown Burgers
desc: A real Utah invention — ask for a lettuce wrap

name: Leku Ona
desc: Oxtail, lamb chops, morcilla. Basque cooking is meat-forward and mostly gluten-free

name: Bar Gernika
desc: Beef tongue is the house dish. Ask for it without the bread

name: Ansots
desc: Basque chorizo to take into the car

name: In-N-Out Burger
desc: Protein style, no cheese. The fries are safe — own fryer, potato and sunflower oil only

name: Eem
desc: Thai barbecue — brisket in curry, and they know their allergens

name: Nong's Khao Man Gai
desc: Chicken and rice. Three ingredients, nothing to go wrong

name: In-N-Out Burger
desc: Protein style, no cheese. The fries are safe — own fryer, potato and sunflower oil only

name: Swan Oyster Depot
desc: Bring cash. Go early or wait

name: Hog Island Oyster Co
desc: Oysters at the Ferry Building with the Bay Bridge behind them. No booking, so go off-peak.

name: Hog Island Oyster Farm
desc: Shuck your own. Reservation essential

name: The Marshall Store
desc: Barbecued oysters on the water

name: In-N-Out Burger Fisherman's Wharf
desc: Protein style, no cheese. The fries are safe — own fryer, potato and sunflower oil only

name: Hama Hama Oyster Saloon
desc: The best oysters of the entire trip, and that includes San Francisco

name: The Martin Hotel
desc: Family-style Basque, and it predates the Boise scene

name: Fields Station
desc: Burger patty, no bun. There is no plan B for a hundred miles

name: Snoqualmie Falls
desc: A 268 ft drop with a viewing platform at the lip, 30 min east of Seattle. A detour on the way out rather than on the way to Rainier.

name: Lake McDonald
desc: Ten miles long, 472 ft deep, and famous for the coloured pebbles you can see straight through the water.

name: Logan Pass
desc: 6,646 ft, the top of Going-to-the-Sun Road, with bighorn sheep on the boardwalk.

name: Many Glacier
desc: The most dramatic basin in Glacier. Flooded and evacuated in June 2026 — confirm it has reopened.

name: Saint Mary Lake
desc: The east side of the park: drier, windier, and Wild Goose Island is the shot everyone knows.

name: Flathead Lake
desc: The largest natural freshwater lake in the western US, and the east shore is lined with cherry stands.

name: National Bison Range
desc: Several hundred bison on a one-way gravel loop you drive from the car.

name: Berkeley Pit
desc: A mile-wide flooded copper mine full of water so acidic it dissolves metal. You pay a dollar to look at it.

name: Museum of the Rockies
desc: Jack Horner's collection — the largest set of T. rex fossils anywhere on Earth. Budget two hours.

name: Mammoth Hot Springs
desc: Travertine terraces that rebuild themselves constantly, with elk bugling through the village in the rut.

name: Lamar Valley
desc: The best wolf watching in the lower 48. Be there before sunrise, not at it.

name: Artist Point
desc: The Lower Falls and the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, from the viewpoint that made the park famous.

name: Grand Prismatic Spring
desc: The largest hot spring in the US. The boardwalk gives you steam; the Fairy Falls overlook gives you the colour.

name: Old Faithful
desc: Erupts every 60–110 minutes to about 130 ft. The prediction board in the visitor centre is accurate.

name: Mormon Row Historic District
desc: The Moulton barns against the Teton range — the most photographed farm buildings in America.

name: Schwabacher Landing
desc: A beaver-dammed side channel that mirrors the whole range. Only works in the first ten minutes of light.

name: Jenny Lake
desc: Glacial, clear, and the shuttle boat cuts two miles off the walk to Hidden Falls. Moose in the willows.

name: Bear Lake
desc: An improbable Caribbean turquoise at 5,900 ft, caused by limestone suspended in the water.

name: Bonneville Salt Flats
desc: Thirty thousand acres of dead-flat salt where land speed records are set. Racing ends Sept 29, so you get it empty.

name: Shoshone Falls
desc: 212 ft — taller than Niagara — though by October the irrigation season has usually taken most of the water.

name: Hagerman Fossil Beds National Monument
desc: Where the Hagerman horse was found: the most complete fossil horse skeleton ever recovered.

name: Multnomah Falls
desc: 620 ft in two tiers, with the Benson footbridge across the middle. The busiest stop in the Gorge.

name: Pike Place Market
desc: Running since 1907. Go early for the fish market, and buy Dungeness crab to eat on the waterfront.

name: Beartooth Pass
desc: 10,947 ft. Switchbacks above the treeline with snowbanks standing into October. Closes Oct 12.

name: Chief Joseph Scenic Byway
desc: WY-296 over Dead Indian Pass, named for the route the Nez Perce took in 1877. Almost nobody drives it.

name: Flaming Gorge Reservoir
desc: Ninety miles of red rock canyon and improbably blue water on the Green River.

name: Dinosaur National Monument
desc: The Quarry Exhibit Hall: 1,500 dinosaur bones left exactly where they were found, in a wall you can touch.

name: Craters of the Moon National Monument
desc: 618 square miles of black lava. Apollo astronauts trained here because it is the closest thing to the Moon.

name: Smith Rock State Park
desc: The birthplace of American sport climbing. Misery Ridge is 45 minutes up for the whole view.

name: Alvord Desert
desc: A dry lake bed you are allowed to drive on, with Steens Mountain rising 5,500 ft straight off it.

name: Alvord Hot Springs
desc: Two tin tubs facing the playa. Privately run, small fee, and about as good as this trip gets.

name: Steens Mountain
desc: A 9,700 ft fault block with a gravel loop road to the top. Golden aspens in early October.

name: Bixby Creek Bridge
desc: A 1932 concrete arch 260 ft above the creek — the most photographed bridge on the Pacific coast.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
desc: Walk or cycle it to Sausalito and take the ferry back. Best light in the late afternoon.

name: Point Reyes Lighthouse
desc: Three hundred steps down a cliff to the foggiest, windiest point on the Pacific coast.

name: Paradise
desc: 5,400 ft, with Mount Rainier another 9,000 ft above you. The Skyline Trail loop is the best day hike in Washington.

name: Hoh Rain Forest
desc: 140 inches of rain a year and moss hanging off everything. The Hall of Mosses is under a mile.

name: Hurricane Ridge
desc: 5,200 ft: the Olympic range on one side, Canada across the strait on the other.

name: Lava Hot Springs
desc: Five pools of mineral water at 43 °C, run by the state and startlingly cheap. Splits the run back to Salt Lake.

name: Antelope Island State Park
desc: A free-roaming herd of about 700 bison on an island in the Great Salt Lake. You float in the water; the smell is part of the deal.

name: Metropolitan Grill
desc: Plain grilled steak, no butter finish. The safest good meal on a jet-lagged arrival night.

name: Staircase, Olympic NP
desc: Olympic National Park's east entrance: old-growth rainforest and the Skokomish rapids, 40 min up from Hoodsport. The real park without the drive to Hoh.

name: Mount Walker Viewpoint
desc: The only drivable summit in the eastern Olympics. One viewpoint looks over Puget Sound to Seattle and Rainier, the other straight into the Olympic range.

name: Port Gamble
desc: An 1853 company mill town preserved essentially intact and listed on the National Register. General store, small museum, and almost nobody there.

name: Hood Canal Bridge
desc: One of the longest floating bridges on Earth at 2.4 km. It swings open sideways to let submarines through to the Bangor base.

name: Lake Cushman
desc: A glacial lake under the Olympics with startlingly clear water, on the way up to Staircase.

name: Washington State Capitol
desc: The tallest self-supporting masonry dome in the US, five minutes off the route, and free to walk into.

name: Crystal Mountain gondola
desc: The highest gondola in Washington, running through autumn, with Rainier filling the whole sky from the top. Ten minutes off the road to Sunrise.

name: Northwest Trek Wildlife Park
desc: A tram tour through 435 free-range acres of bison, elk, moose, caribou and bighorn sheep. A useful warm-up for Yellowstone, and it is directly on the road from Ashford.

name: Ballard Locks
desc: A working ship canal with a glass-walled fish ladder underneath it. Late September is the tail of the salmon run, so you can watch them climb.

name: Kerry Park
desc: The postcard view: Space Needle, downtown and Mount Rainier stacked behind each other. Tiny park, five minutes, best at dusk.

name: Museum of Flight
desc: Far better than it sounds: the first Air Force One, a Concorde, an SR-71 and the original Boeing factory. Good rainy-day insurance.

name: HP Garage — birthplace of Silicon Valley
desc: 367 Addison Avenue: the garage where Hewlett and Packard started with $538 in 1938. Every trillion-dollar campus you will see today descends from this shed.

name: Apple Park Visitor Center
desc: The $5B ring seen from the Visitor Center roof terrace, with an AR model of the campus. Started in a garage nine kilometres from here.

name: Googleplex & Android Garden
desc: The campus that grew out of a Stanford dorm project. The Android lawn statues are the photo stop; the Gradient Canopy building is the architecture stop.

name: Computer History Museum
desc: Abacus to transistor to web in two hours. The single best stop of the day for reframing what a garage-sized idea can become.

name: Meta HQ — 1 Hacker Way
desc: The thumbs-up sign at the entrance is the classic five-minute photo. The back of the sign still carries Sun Microsystems' logo — a deliberate memento mori.

name: Tesla Fremont Factory
desc: The plant GM and Toyota walked away from, now building the Model Y you just drove 3,000 km. Visible from Fremont Blvd; tours are rare but the scale reads from outside.

name: Stanford University
desc: Walk the Main Quad and Memorial Church. Google, HP, Nvidia, Netflix and Instagram all trace back to people who walked these arcades.

name: Salesforce Park
desc: A public park on a roof four storeys above the street, threaded between towers. The gondola up from Fremont Street is free.

name: Muir Woods
desc: Thousand-year-old coast redwoods twenty minutes from the bridge. Parking is reservation-only — book before you go.

name: Sausalito
desc: Houseboats, a waterfront, and the best view of the San Francisco skyline there is. Take the ferry back instead of driving.

name: Mount Tamalpais East Peak
desc: 784 m above the whole Bay Area, a paved road almost to the top. On a clear day you see the Farallon Islands 50 km out to sea.
